pages.title: Affiliate Groups
pages.content:
AffiliateWP allows you to organize your affiliates into groups and apply custom referral rates based on group membership. This gives you more control and flexibility in managing commission structures across different types of affiliates.

In This Article

- [Managing Affiliate Groups](#managing-affiliate-groups)
- [Adding a New Affiliate Group](#adding-a-new-affiliate-group)
- [Assigning Affiliates to a Group](#assigning-affiliates-to-a-group)
- [How Group Rates Affect Referrals](#how-group-rates-affect-referrals)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)- [Can I automatically assign new affiliates to a group?](#can-i-automatically-assign-new-affiliates-to-a-group)

## Managing Affiliate Groups

To manage affiliate groups, navigate to **AffiliateWP » Affiliates » Groups** in your WordPress admin dashboard. Here you can view, create, and manage all affiliate groups for your site.

Each group displays key information including the group name, description, referral rate, rate type, and the number of affiliates in the group. Clicking the **Count** value will take you to a filtered list of affiliates belonging to that group.

## Adding a New Affiliate Group

To add a new group, fill out the **Add New Group** form on the Groups screen:

- **Name**: Enter a name for the group. This name is visible in both the admin and affiliate management areas.
- **Description**: Optionally add a description. This is for internal reference only and does not appear publicly.
- **Set this group as the default group for new affiliates**: Enable this option to automatically assign all newly registered affiliates to this group.
- **Enable custom rate for all affiliates in this group**: Enable this to apply a group-wide referral rate that overrides global and per-affiliate settings.

![Add new group](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/add-new-group-767x761.png)

If a custom rate is enabled for the group, you can then configure:

- **Referral Rate**: The specific commission amount (e.g., 20 or 15%).
- **Rate Type**: Choose whether the rate is a **percentage** or a **flat amount**.
- **Flat Rate Basis** (if applicable): If the rate type is set to *Flat*, choose whether the rate applies per product sold or per order.

Once saved, the group will appear in the Affiliate Groups list.

![Group list](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/group-list-767x150.png)

## Assigning Affiliates to a Group

To assign an affiliate to a group:

1. Navigate to **AffiliateWP » Affiliates**.
2. Click on the name of the affiliate you want to edit.
3. On the edit screen, scroll below the **Affiliate Status** section to the **Group** dropdown.
4. Select the desired group from the available options and click **Update Affiliate**.

![Add affiliate to group](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/add-affiliate-to-group-767x183.png)

An affiliate can only be assigned to **one group at a time**. They cannot belong to multiple groups.

Once assigned, the affiliate’s group is displayed in the main Affiliates list. A visual notice will also appear next to their referral rate, indicating that the affiliate is part of a group and that the group’s rate settings may override individual rates.

![Affiliate group notice](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Pasted_Image_01_08_2025__8_09 AM-767x201.png)

This notice is also visible when editing the affiliate’s profile.

## How Group Rates Affect Referrals

When an affiliate belongs to a group that has a custom referral rate enabled, the group rate will:

- Override the global referral rate
- Override the affiliate-specific referral rate

This ensures that all affiliates within the group follow a consistent commission structure.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can affiliates belong to more than one group?

No. Each affiliate can only be assigned to one group at a time.

### What takes priority: group rates or affiliate-specific rates?

Group-level referral rates override both the global rate and any individual affiliate-specific rates.

### Can I automatically assign new affiliates to a group?

Yes. When creating a group, enable the **Set this group as the default** option. New affiliates will then be automatically added to that group upon registration.

---

And that’s it! Now you can organize your affiliates in groups and set more granular custom rates for those groups.
headings: Can affiliates belong to more than one group?
What takes priority: group rates or affiliate-specific rates?
Can I automatically assign new affiliates to a group?

pages.title: Canceling Your Account
pages.content:
Would you like to cancel your auto-renewal for AffiliateWP? Whether you no longer want to use our plugin or wish to renew your license manually, you can easily manage your subscription from your account.

In this tutorial, we’ll show you how to turn off auto-renewal for your AffiliateWP subscription to cancel your account.

- [Canceling Your AffiliateWP Subscription](/docs/how-to-cancel-your-affiliatewp-account/#cancel)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](/docs/how-to-cancel-your-affiliatewp-account/#faq)

---

## Canceling Your AffiliateWP Subscription

AffiliateWP is a subscription-based product with an annual license. By default, your subscription will be set to auto-renew each year.

When you cancel your subscription, you’ll be able to finish out your paid term until the renewal date listed in your account. At the end of that period, you can choose to manually renew your license or just let it expire if you no longer need AffiliateWP.

To cancel your subscription, you’ll first need to [log in to your AffiliateWP Account](https://affiliatewp.com/account).

If you would like to check your license’s renewal date before proceeding, click on the **Downloads** tab.

Look for your license in the list, then check the **Renewal Date** section of the table.

![Viewing the renewal date](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/view-renewal-date-1024x543.png)

Next, click on the **Billing** tab. This page will display all of your previous license payments, and all of your active subscriptions. To cancel auto-renewal on any license, scroll down to the **Subscriptions**section, then select **Cancel**.

![Clicking to cancel the subscription](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/cancel-license-renewal-1024x452.png)

After clicking this link, you’ll see a page asking if the AffiliateWP team can assist further. You can choose **Yes, I’d like to get VIP Support!** if you’d like to contact support for assistance, or you can choose **No thanks, continue cancelling** to proceed with the cancellation.

Select the option that makes the most sense for you.

### Getting Help from Support

If you decide that you’d like to get help from support, you’ll be linked to our contact form. Here you can share all of the details on how our team can best help out.

![AffiliateWP support form](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/support-form-1024x625.png)

Complete all the required fields and click the **Submit** button at the bottom of the screen. Our support team will reach out to you as soon as possible to discuss your issue and help you resolve it.

### Continuing with Cancellation

If you decide to continue with the cancellation process, you’ll be asked a couple of short questions to help improve AffiliateWP. You must complete this form in order to cancel your renewal.

![Choosing a reason for canceling your AffiliateWP license](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/why-do-you-want-to-cancel-1024x535.png)

Once you submit your reason for canceling, we’ll show you a list of all the paid features that you’ll lose when you no longer have access to your license. If you’re sure you want to proceed, select the **Yes, I understand I will lose all the above when my plan expires** checkbox. Then click **Continue Cancelling**.

![Agreeing to lose AffiliateWP paid features when you cancel your license](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/understand-lose-all-of-the-above-when-license-expires-1024x327.png)

Finally, you’ll see a confirmation page with your license expiration date, another summary of the benefits you’ll lose after your license expires, and a note reminding you that you’ll still have access to your existing features and addons.

Click **Confirm Cancellation** to proceed and finish the process.

![Confirming your AffiliateWP cancellation](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/confirm-affiliatewp-cancellation-921x1024.png)

## Frequently Asked Questions

These are some of the top questions we see about canceling AffiliateWP licenses.

### Can I get a refund?

The AffiliateWP no-risk money back guarantee offers that, if at any time within the first 14 days of opening your paid Account you decide that AffiliateWP is not for you, then just let our awesome support team know (we make it easy!).

### Can I continue using AffiliateWP if I cancel my license?

If you cancel your AffiliateWP license, you’ll still have access to your existing affiliates, referrals and more. However, you will no longer receive plugin updates.

This prevents you from accessing new features and can lead to potential security risks.

That’s it! Now you know everything you need to cancel your AffiliateWP license.

If we can answer any other questions about your subscription, please [get in touch with our support team](https://affiliatewp.com/contact/) and we’ll be happy to help!
headings: Can I continue using AffiliateWP if I cancel my license?

pages.title: Upgrading Your License
pages.content:
Do you want to unlock all of the awesome AffiliateWP features that come with a higher license level? Each license in AffiliateWP comes with additional features that let you add even more functionality to your affiliate program.

Whether you’re looking to use AffiliateWP on more websites, or you want to access our other premium addons, this tutorial will walk you through how to upgrade your AffiliateWP account.

In This Article

- [Accessing Upgrades](#access-upgrades)
- [Understanding Pro-Rated Upgrade Pricing](#prorated-pricing)
- [Completing Your License Upgrade](#complete-upgrade)

---

## Accessing Upgrades

The first step to upgrade your license is to [log into your AffiliateWP account](https://affiliatewp.com/account/). Once you’ve logged in, click on the **Downloads** tab.

![Click the Downloads Tab](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/downloads-tab-in-affiliatewp-1024x317.png)

On the Downloads page, you’ll see your current license details. If you’re upgrading from a Personal or Plus license level, click the **Expand to see Available Addons and Download Links** option.

![Expand to see Available Addons and Download Links](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/download-links-upgrade-2-1024x327.png)

This will expand to show you additional features you can unlock with the Pro license. To upgrade, go ahead and click on the **Upgrade to AffiliateWP Pro** button.

![Upgrade to AffiliateWP Pro Plan](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/upgrade-to-affiliatewp-pro-1-1024x277.png)

## Understanding Pro-Rated Upgrade Pricing

On the Upgrades page, you’ll see a list of our available licenses, and the cost of upgrading for each.

All upgrade costs are pro-rated, so the prices you see will be based on both your current license level, as well as how much time is left in your current subscription. This means that you only pay for the time that you use the upgrade.

Here’s how pro-rated costs are calculated:

1. **You’ll only pay the difference:** This means that if you’re upgrading from a Personal License ($299) to a Pro License ($599), the difference for a full year would be $300.
2. **This cost is pro-rated by time:** For example, if you only have 6 months left in your license, then you’ll only pay half of the upgrade cost.
3. **BONUS – Additional 50% discount:** We’re currently offering an additional 50% off of the pro-rated price, automatically applied to all upgrades at checkout.

When you’ve decided which license you’d like, click the **Upgrade** button underneath that specific license level. This will take you to the checkout page, where you can complete your purchase.

**Note:** When the time comes to renew your annual subscription, you will be charged the standard renewal rate for your license level.

## Completing Your License Upgrade

Once you’ve purchased your license upgrade, open up your WordPress admin area and go to **AffiliateWP » Settings**.

From here, you can view your current license level under the **License Key** field. If you don’t see the name of your upgraded license, be sure to click **Deactivate License** and then **Activate License** again.

![Deactivate AffiliateWP license](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/license-level-1024x380.png)

That’s it, you’ve upgraded your AffiliateWP license!

Now that you’ve completed your upgrade, you’ll have access to more features and addons. To learn more about how to set these up, check out our full list of [addon tutorials](/doc-categories/addons/).

pages.title: Updating Your Billing Details
pages.content:
Do you need to change billing information for your AffiliateWP account? Keeping your payment details up to date will help ensure that your license renews successfully.

In this tutorial, we’ll show you how to change or update the billing information for your AffiliateWP account.

- [Updating Credit Card Details](#credit-card)
- [Updating PayPal Details](#paypal)

**Note:** Billing updates will work differently depending on whether you’ve selected Credit Card or PayPal on the AffiliateWP checkout page.

---

## Updating Credit Card Details

To get started, you’ll need to [log into your AffiliateWP account](https://affiliatewp.com/account).

Once logged in, you’ll need to click on the **Billing** tab. Then, on the right side, click the **Update Payment Methods** button.

![The Update Payment Methods button](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/affiliatewp-update-payment-methods.png)

**Note:** If you do not see the **Update Payment Methods** option, this means that you paid through [PayPal](#paypal).

Clicking this button will open up a pop-up form where you can view the current card on file.

![Payment Methods in AffiliateWP account](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/account-billing-payment-methods.png)

From here, you can update, delete, or add a new card. If you’d like to add a new credit card to your account, click the **Add New card** button.

![The Add New Card button](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/account-billing-payment-methods-add-card.png)

This will open a form allowing you to add your new credit card details. Once you complete the form, be sure to click the **Add New Card** button to add the details to your account.

![Click Add New Card](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/account-billing-payment-methods-add-card-filled.png)

If the card has been added successfully, a message will appear that reads **Card successfully added**.

## Updating PayPal Details

If you paid with PayPal, all payment details will be handled within your PayPal account. To update this information, please check out [PayPal’s guide to managing payment methods](https://www.paypal.com/us/smarthelp/article/how-do-i-link,-remove,-or-change-a-credit-card-or-prepaid-card-faq1457).

That’s it! We hope this guide helped you to easily update your billing details.

If you have any additional questions about your account, [please get in touch with our support team](/contact/). We’d be happy to assist!

Next, would you like to renew your AffiliateWP license? Make sure to check out our tutorial on [renewing your license](/docs/how-to-renew-your-affiliatewp-license/) for all the details.

pages.title: Renewing Your License
pages.content:
Are you trying to renew your AffiliateWP license, but not sure how? Making sure your license stays active ensures you have access to important plugin updates.

In this tutorial we’ll show you the steps to renew any AffiliateWP license.

In This Article

- [Renewing an Expired License](#renew-expired)
- [Resolving a Failing Renewal Payment Issue](#failing-renewal)
- [Renewing a License Before it Expires](#renew-before-expired)

## Renewing an Expired License

In order to renew your license after it’s expired, you’ll first need to [open up your AffiliateWP account](https://affiliatewp.com/account/).

If a license in your account has expired, you should see an expiration notice on the right side of this page. In this notice, click the **Renew your license** link.

![Click the Renew your license button on the Overview tab](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/account-renew-license-button.png)

If you don’t see this expiration notice, you can instead click on the **Downloads** tab.

To the right of your license type, you should see a red button labeled **Renew AffiliateWP**.

![Click the Renew AffiliateWP button on the Downloads tab](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/account-downloads-renew-affiliatewp-button.png)

After clicking this renewal button, a checkout page will appear. Here, you can choose a payment method and complete the renewal.

![Checkout page for AffiliateWP license renewal - AffiliateWP](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/checkout-renew-license.png)

Once you’ve completed the checkout process, your license will be renewed.

## Resolving a Failing Renewal Payment Issue

If your license’s auto-renewal isn’t able to be processed for any reason, then you should receive an email from our team letting you know about the issue. When this happens, your license will also expire until you have a chance to update your payment details.

To get things back on track, please follow our guide to [update your account’s payment information](http://how-to-update-billing-details-for-your-affiliatewp-account/).

Please also note that, if you’re paying with a credit card, it may take a day or more before the payment attempts to run again. [Please reach out to our support team](https://affiliatewp.com/account/support/) if you’d like to manually trigger the charge right away.

## Renewing a License Before it Expires

If your license hasn’t expired yet, then in most cases you can simply wait until it does expire before you renew it. Then, you can follow [the steps above](#renew-expired).

**Note:** This section only applies if you have manually cancelled the auto-renewal on your subscription. There is currently no way to renew early by directly visiting your AffiliateWP account. The only early renewal option is through the special email link described below.

However, there is another option if you’d like to renew your license slightly early. Your renewal reminder emails will include a special renewal link, and clicking this will allow you to renew your license ahead of time.

![Early renewal notice - AffiliateWP](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/renewal-email-1.png)

The first renewal reminder email will be sent to you 30 days before your license is set to expire.
headings: Resolving a Failing Renewal Payment Issue
Renewing a License Before it Expires

pages.title: How to Customize the Affiliate Registration Form
pages.content:
Want to create an affiliate registration form with content specific to your website?  You can do this using the WordPress block editor (formerly known as Gutenberg) along with the Affiliate Registration block to create and customize the affiliate registration form to your liking.  If you are not familiar with using the block editor, you can view this tutorial on [how to use blocks in WordPress](https://www.wpbeginner.com/beginners-guide/how-to-use-the-new-wordpress-block-editor/).

In this tutorial we’ll show you how to add, remove, or rearrange fields, change field labels, make specific fields required, or not required, change the Register Button text, and more. Let’s get started!

1. [Add the affiliate registration block to your page](#add-affiliate-registration-block-to-page)
2. [AffiliateWP block vs Affiliate Registration block vs [affiliate_area] shortcode](#affiliatewp-block-vs-affiliate-registration-block)
3. [Customize default fields](#customize-default-fields)
4. [Remove default fields](#remove-default-fields)
5. [Add new fields](#add-new-fields)
6. [Change Register button text](#change-register-button-text)
7. [FAQs](#faqs)

---

### 1. Add the affiliate registration block to your page

Once you’ve opened the page editor, you can add a new block by clicking the plus (+) icon in the upper left corner.

![screenshot of plus sign to bring up block options](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-plus-to-open-menu-of-block-options-1024x213.png)

This will open a menu of block options. You can add a new affiliate registration form by typing “Affiliate” in your blocks search bar.

![screenshot of typing in text in the search bar for blocks](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/type-affiliate-in-blocks-search-bar-1024x416.png)

Then select Affiliate Registration. This will add the default AffiliateWP registration form to your page, and you can begin to customize it if desired.

![screenshot of selecting the Affiliate Registration block](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/select-affiliate-registration-from-menu-1024x378.png)

### 2. Affiliate Area block vs Affiliate Registration block vs [affiliate_area] shortcode

Until version Version 2.9.4 of AffiliateWP released on May 13, 2022,  when you first installed  and activated AffiliateWP, an affiliate-area page was created with a single [affiliate_area] shortcode on the page.

**Note**: If you are not sure how your affiliate-area page was constructed, you can always click to edit the page to check in your WordPress admin – Pages menu.

By default, the shortcode will display both the Affiliate Registration and Affiliate Login forms.  This of course can be changed based on your Affiliate Form Shortcode Settings found in **AffiliateWP » Settings » General**

![screenshot of the affiliate form shortcode settings](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/affiliate-form-shortcode-settings-1024x169.png)

**Note**: The settings above, as well as the **Required Registration Fields**section, only apply when using the [affiliate_area] shortcode.  Those settings do not apply when using blocks as you would instead make those changes directly on the page by removing the form you did not want, making fields required, etc.

If your affiliate-area page still contains the shortcode and you’d like to switch to blocks, you can remove the  [affiliate_area] shortcode from the page, and add the Affiliate Area block.  You would follow the same steps as you did to [add the affiliate registration in the previous section](#add-affiliate-registration-block-to-page), except this time choose the Affiliate Area block.

![screenshot of selecting the Affiliate Area block from the search](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/select-affiliate-area-from-menu-1024x378.png)

The Affiliate Area block is a group block that contains both the Affiliate Registration and Affiliate Login blocks.

![screenshot of the full Affiliate Area block that includes the Affiliate Registration and Affiliate Login form blocks](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/affiliate-area-block-editor-950x1024.png)

Notice the default affiliate registration form does not include the password fields, but no worries, we’ll show you how to add these easily in the [Add new fields section](#add-new-fields), but first, let’s get you comfortable customizing the default fields.

### 3. Customize default fields

Now that you have the basic fields, you can begin to make changes.  For example, if you’d like the **Payment Email** field to be required, you can click anywhere inside the field or field label to display the field settings on the right side of your screen.

![screenshot of the Payment Email with the cursor within](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-payment-email-field-1024x212.png)

Next, slide the Required slide to the right to turn on, and this will add *(*required*)*to the field label automatically.

![screenshot of the Field settings Required slider in the block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-require-payment-email-1024x454.png)

While in that same field settings area, you can also change the label in the FIELD LABEL field, perhaps to something like PayPal Email.  You can also add placeholder text just below that as well in the FIELD PLACEHOLDER field.

### 4. Remove default fields

If there are fields on the default affiliate registration block that simply don’t apply, feel free to remove them!  For example, if you’d like to remove the **Website URL**field, click anywhere in the field label or field contents, then click the 3 dot ellipses.

![screenshot of selecting the 3 dot elipses](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-3-dot-ellipses-1024x219.png)

Select the field name to remove at the bottom.

![screenshot of removing a field in the block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-remove-field-1024x352.png)

### 5. Add new fields

Adding new fields to the affiliate registration form is one of the most popular requests we receive in support.  You can probably see by now that it’s going to be painless using blocks.

Let’s start by showing you how to add the Password fields. The fields are connected to the parent block, so first make sure you’ve got the affiliate registration form selected.

![screenshot of selecting a parent block in the block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/select-affiliate-registration-block-1024x272.png)

Now at the bottom+right of the affiliate registration form you should see a plus sign, and click to see the available fields that can be added.

![screenshot of the plus sign to add a field to a form in the block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/plus-sign-bottom-right-of-affiliate-registration-form-1024x325.png)

Select the Password field to add it to the form (the Confirm Password field will also be added automatically.)

![screenshot of selecting the Password field in the available fields for the Affiliate Registration form block](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/add-password-to-affiliate-registration-1024x479.png)

Then, you can use the arrows to position the fields up or down within the registration form to where you’d like them to be.

![screenshot showing the up/down arrows of block placement on the page](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/use-the-arrows-to-position-up-or-down-1024x416.png)

Click to save your changes on the page.

![screenshot of the Update button in the page/block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/click-update-to-save-changes-1024x227.png)

### 6. Change Register button text

The default label for the button to submit the affiliate registration form is **Register**, but you can easily change that as well.   Click on the button, then change the text in the BUTTON TEXT field to what you prefer.

![screenshot of the settings for a button using the block editor](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/change-register-button-text-1-1024x439.png)

### 7. FAQs

Can I put my affiliate registration form on a separate page?Yes! Your Affiliate Registration block does not have to reside on the Affiliate Area page, it can be on the page of your choice.  Think of this as the equivalent to using the [affiliate_registration] shortcode on a separate page before blocks were available. The same applies to the Affiliate Login block as well, the related shortcode for that used to be [affiliate_login].

Can I have more than one affiliate registration form?Yes!  With blocks this is now possible. You can place Affiliate Registration blocks on as many pages as you like, and each one can be configured differently if preferred.

Can I rearrange the default fields on the affiliate registration form?Yes, you can move the default fields, or any field, up or down in any position you like using the up/down directional arrows in the block/field settings.

![](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/faq-how-to-rearrange-fields-with-move-arrows-1024x250.png)

That’s it! You can now customize the Affiliate Registration Form using the WordPress block editor. Next, have a look at additional ways to add new affiliates to rev up your affiliate program:  [Adding new affiliate accounts](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/adding-new-affiliate-accounts/)
headings: 1. Add the affiliate registration block to your page
2. Affiliate Area block vs Affiliate Registration block vs [affiliate_area] shortcode

pages.title: Setting Up Google reCAPTCHA
pages.content:
Are spam registrations becoming a problem for your affiliate program? Google’s reCAPTCHA is a powerful tool for preventing spam and fraudulent activity on your affiliate registration forms. By integrating reCAPTCHA with AffiliateWP, you can protect your forms from automated bots while maintaining a smooth experience for legitimate users.

This guide will walk you through setting up Google reCAPTCHA in AffiliateWP and ensuring it works correctly on your registration forms.

In This Article

- [Configuring reCAPTCHA Type](#recaptcha-type)
- [Generating reCAPTCHA Keys in Google](#generating-recaptcha-keys-in-google)
- [Adding reCAPTCHA to the Login Form](#adding-recaptcha-to-the-login-form)
- [Testing reCAPTCHA](#testing-recaptcha)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)

## Configuring reCAPTCHA Type

To begin, log in to your WordPress site and navigate to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Affiliates**. Scroll down to the **Affiliate Registration & Login Security** section. Under the CAPTCHA options, select **Google reCAPTCHA**.

![Google reCAPTCHA](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/select-recaptcha-767x295.png)

Once selected, you’ll be able to choose the type of reCAPTCHA you want to use:

- **reCAPTCHA v2**: Adds a checkbox labeled “I’m not a robot” to your registration form.
- **reCAPTCHA v3**: Runs invisibly in the background, using behavior analysis to detect spam.

Choose the option that works best for your site.

## Generating reCAPTCHA Keys in Google

Once you’ve chosen a reCAPTCHA type, visit the [Google reCAPTCHA site](https://www.google.com/recaptcha/admin/create) to generate the necessary keys.

1. Log in with your Google account and click the **+ Add** button to register your site.
2. Select the reCAPTCHA type (v2 or v3) that matches your AffiliateWP settings.
3. Add your domain(s). Ensure all variations, such as 
```
www.yourdomain.com
```

 and 
```
yourdomain.com
```

, are included.
4. Agree to the terms of service and click Submit.

![Register site ](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-767x449.png)

#### Retrieving and Adding Keys

Google will generate a **Site Key** and **Secret Key**. Copy these keys and paste them into their respective fields in **AffiliateWP » Settings » Affiliates**.

![reCAPTCHA verssion](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-key-767x308.png)

If you’re using reCAPTCHA v3, the Score Threshold setting determines how strictly reCAPTCHA filters suspicious behavior.

- A **lower threshold** (e.g., 0.3) is less strict, allowing more registrations but potentially letting some spam through.
- A **higher threshold** (e.g., 0.7) is stricter, reducing spam but potentially blocking legitimate users.

Adjust this setting as needed, then click **Save Changes** to apply.

## Adding reCAPTCHA to the Login Form

After selecting reCAPTCHA, you’ll also see a checkbox labeled Add CAPTCHA to Affiliate Login form.

![Add CAPTCHA to Affiliate login form](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/captcha-login-form-1-767x96.png)

Select this option if you’d like to apply reCAPTCHA protection to the login form as well. This helps block automated login attempts and strengthens overall security.

Don’t forget to save your changes after enabling this option.

## Testing reCAPTCHA

After completing setup, it’s important to confirm that reCAPTCHA is working correctly on both the registration and login forms.

### Testing the Registration Form

If you’re using **reCAPTCHA v2**, go to your affiliate registration page and verify that the **“I’m not a robot”** checkbox appears. Complete the form and submit a test registration to ensure it works as expected.

![reCAPTCHA V2](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-registration-767x313.png)

If you’re using **reCAPTCHA v3**, visit the registration page and check that the reCAPTCHA **badge appears in the bottom-right corner** of the page. Submit a test registration to confirm that submissions are processed without errors. No user interaction is required with v3.

![reCAPTCHA v3](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-v3-registration-767x210.png)

### Testing the Login Form

If you enabled the **Add CAPTCHA to Affiliate Login form** option in your settings, reCAPTCHA will also apply to the affiliate login page.

With reCAPTCHA v2, the login form will display the “I’m not a robot” checkbox. You may be prompted to complete an image challenge if Google suspects suspicious behavior.

![reCAPTCHA v2 login form](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-login-767x337.png)

With reCAPTCHA v3, there will be no visual CAPTCHA on the login form. Instead, reCAPTCHA will evaluate the login attempt silently using your configured Score Threshold.

![reCAPTCHA V3 login form](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/recaptcha-login-v3-767x245.png)

If everything looks and functions correctly, your registration forms are now protected.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I use reCAPTCHA for other forms on my WordPress site?

The reCAPTCHA integration in AffiliateWP is specifically designed for affiliate registration forms. To protect other forms, such as contact forms or comment sections, you’ll need to use a WordPress plugin that supports global reCAPTCHA integration, like WPForms or Contact Form 7.

### Does reCAPTCHA v3 block all suspicious users?

No, reCAPTCHA v3 provides a **spam score** based on user behavior. It’s up to your settings (Score Threshold) to decide how strict the filtering is. Lower thresholds are more permissive, while higher thresholds are stricter, potentially blocking more users, including some legitimate ones.

### Is reCAPTCHA compatible with caching plugins?

Yes, reCAPTCHA is generally compatible with caching plugins. However, ensure that dynamic pages, like your affiliate registration form, are excluded from caching to avoid conflicts.

### How do I know reCAPTCHA is working?

You can test reCAPTCHA by visiting your registration form as a new user. For v2, ensure the “I’m not a robot” checkbox or image challenge appears. For v3, check for the badge in the bottom-right corner of the page and ensure registrations are processed correctly.

### Will enabling reCAPTCHA impact my affiliate conversions?

When configured correctly, reCAPTCHA minimizes spam without negatively affecting conversions. Using v3 ensures a seamless experience for legitimate users, as they won’t need to interact with a CAPTCHA.

### What happens if I switch from reCAPTCHA v2 to v3 (or vice versa)?

If you switch reCAPTCHA types, you must update the Site Key and Secret Key in AffiliateWP settings. Testing your registration form after the switch ensures the new setup works correctly.

### What should I do if reCAPTCHA is not displaying on my form?

If reCAPTCHA isn’t appearing:

- Check for JavaScript errors or conflicts with other plugins or themes.
- Ensure the correct Site Key and Secret Key are added to AffiliateWP settings.
- Verify your registration form is active and using the correct page.

---

That’s it! Google reCAPTCHA is a powerful tool for safeguarding your affiliate registration forms against spam and fraud. Whether you choose the interactive protection of v2 or the seamless background monitoring of v3, enabling reCAPTCHA ensures a smoother, more secure experience for legitimate users.

pages.title: Tutor LMS
pages.content:
AffiliateWP allows you to reward your affiliates with referrals for course registrations using Tutor LMS through the integration of Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce. This guide will show you how to set up and use Tutor LMS with AffiliateWP to track and reward referrals effectively.

In This Article

- [Integrating Tutor LMS](#aioseo-enable-woocommerce)- [For Easy Digital Downloads](#for-easy-digital-downloads)
- [For WooCommerce:](#for-woocommerce)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#aioseo-frequently-asked-questions)

To use AffiliateWP with Tutor LMS, you must first use either [Easy Digital Downloads](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/easy-digital-downloads/)or [WooCommerce](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/woocommerce/) as your eCommerce platform. Both of these platforms integrate seamlessly with AffiliateWP.

## Integrating Tutor LMS

To track course sales and referrals in **Tutor LMS**, AffiliateWP connects through your chosen eCommerce platform — either **Easy Digital Downloads (EDD)** or **WooCommerce**. Once one of these integrations is enabled, AffiliateWP will automatically record referrals when a course is purchased.

#### For Easy Digital Downloads

1. Navigate to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Integrations**.
2. Select **Easy Digital Downloads**.
3. Click **Save Changes**.

![Enable EDD Integration](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/affiliatewp-edd-integration-767x575.png)

#### For WooCommerce:

1. Navigate to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Integrations**.
2. Select **WooCommerce**.
3. Click **Save Changes**.

![Enable WooCommerce Integration](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/affiliatewp-woocommerce-integration-767x533.png)

Once you have Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce set up and integrated with AffiliateWP, you can move on to integrating Tutor LMS. Tutor LMS works well with both platforms, so any courses sold will generate a referral through AffiliateWP. You can follow the specific instructions for integrating Tutor LMS with your chosen eCommerce platform:

- [Using Tutor LMS with Easy Digital Downloads](https://docs.themeum.com/tutor-lms/ecommerce/easy-digital-download/)
- [Using Tutor LMS with WooCommerce](https://docs.themeum.com/tutor-lms/ecommerce/woocommerce/)

Since Tutor LMS connects with both Easy Digital Downloads and WooCommerce, and AffiliateWP has direct integrations with these platforms, you can be confident that any courses sold will generate a referral. This setup helps you manage and reward your affiliates easily.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need to use Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce with Tutor LMS?

Yes, to use AffiliateWP with Tutor LMS, you need to use either Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce as your eCommerce platform. These platforms integrate directly with AffiliateWP to track and manage referrals.

### Will AffiliateWP track referrals for all courses sold through Tutor LMS?

Yes, as long as you have integrated Tutor LMS with Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce and enabled the integration in AffiliateWP, all courses sold will generate a referral.

---

That’s it! By integrating Tutor LMS with AffiliateWP through Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce, you can track and reward referrals for course registrations. This integration helps you manage your affiliate program and boost your marketing efforts by leveraging your affiliates’ networks.

pages.title: Fraud Prevention addon
pages.content:
Affiliate fraud can be a significant challenge, impacting the profitability and integrity of your affiliate program. The AffiliateWP Fraud Prevention addon provides advanced tools to help you detect and prevent fraudulent activity within your program. This addon introduces additional layers of protection, allowing you to closely monitor affiliate behavior and take action against suspicious activities.

In this article, we’ll walk you through the process of installing the Fraud Prevention addon and configuring its features to enhance the security of your affiliate program.

In This Article

- [Installing the Fraud Prevention Addon](#installing-fraud-prevention)
- [Using Fraud Prevention](#using-fraud-prevention)- [Self-Referrals](#aioseo-self-referrals)
- [Conversion Rate](#aioseo-conversion-rate)
- [Referring Sites](#aioseo-referring-sites)
- [Viewing Flagged Referrals](#aioseo-conversion-rate)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#aioseo-frequently-asked-questions)

**Requirements:** You will need a [Pro license](https://affiliatewp.com/pricing/) to access the Fraud Prevention add-on.

---

## Installing the Fraud Prevention Addon

Before we get started, be sure to [install and activate AffiliateWP](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/how-to-install-the-affiliatewp-plugin/) on your WordPress site.

Once you’ve got AffiliateWP installed and [your license is verified](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/how-to-verify-your-affiliatewp-license/), you’ll be able to quickly [install and activate the Fraud Prevention addon](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/how-to-install-and-activate-affiliatewp-add-ons/).

## Using Fraud Prevention

After activating the Fraud Prevention addon, the **Anti-Fraud** tab will appear under **AffiliateWP » Settings**. Here, you’ll find several features designed to help you minimize fraud within your affiliate program.

### Self-Referrals

The Self-Referrals setting controls whether affiliates can earn commissions on their purchases using their own affiliate links or coupon codes. If you allow self-referrals, affiliates will be able to generate commissions on their purchases.

If you prefer to monitor self-referrals more closely, you can select the **Flag** option. This allows affiliates to generate self-referrals, but these will be flagged for review. The flagged referrals are still eligible for payout, but the flag will help you identify and investigate any potentially suspicious activity.

![Self Referrals](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/self-referrals-1024x212.png)

Alternatively, you can choose the **Reject** option, which is the default setting for AffiliateWP without any addons. This setting prevents affiliates from earning commissions on their purchases entirely, thus blocking self-referrals.

If you have the **Allow Own Referrals** addon active, it will automatically set the Self-Referrals option to **Allow** and disable the **Flag** and **Reject** options. A note at the bottom of the Self-Referrals section will indicate that the **Allow Own Referrals** addon is active. To enable flagging or rejecting self-referrals, you’ll need to deactivate this addon.

![Self Referrals Allow Own Referral addon](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/self-referral-allow-own-referral-addon-1024x212.png)

### Conversion Rate

The Conversion Rate feature monitors an affiliate’s conversion rate, which is the ratio of referrals to visits, to ensure it falls within a specified range. This check is applied once the affiliate has generated at least 10 referrals.

![Conversion Rate](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/conversion-rate-1-1024x186.png)

Selecting the **Allow** option means that affiliates can generate referrals regardless of their conversion rate.

If you choose the **Flag** option, visits and referrals will be flagged as potentially fraudulent if the affiliate’s conversion rate falls outside the defined limits. These flagged referrals are still eligible for payout but should be reviewed.

When **Flag** is selected, two input fields will appear, allowing you to set the minimum and maximum conversion rates that are considered acceptable.

![Conversion Rate Flag options](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/flag-options-1024x445.png)

### Referring Sites

The Referring Sites feature checks whether the URL that referred the visit matches the affiliate’s registered website URL.

![Referring Sites](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/referring-sites-1024x214.png)

If you choose the **Allow** option, affiliates can generate a visit and referral from any referring site URL, even if it doesn’t match the one provided during their application.

If you select the **Flag** option, affiliates can still generate visits and referrals, but if the referring site does not match the affiliate’s registered URL, those visits and referrals will be flagged as potentially fraudulent. These flagged entries are eligible for payout but should be reviewed.

If you prefer stricter control, the **Reject** option ensures that visits from non-matching URLs are not recorded, meaning no referral will be generated if the referring site does not match the affiliate’s registered URL.

When using the Referring Sites setting, please consider that some external sites might not provide a referring URL due to specific link formatting. This could lead to legitimate referrals being flagged or rejected, so it’s important to configure this setting based on your specific needs.

## Viewing Flagged Referrals

When a referral is flagged by the Fraud Prevention addon, it will be visibly marked with a red flag icon in **AffiliateWP » Referrals**.

![Flagged referral](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/flagged-referral-767x146.png)

Hovering over this icon will provide a message explaining which fraud prevention setting triggered the alert.

This feature allows you to quickly identify and investigate any referrals that might be suspicious, ensuring you maintain the integrity of your affiliate program.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the purpose of the Fraud Prevention addon?

The Fraud Prevention addon helps protect your affiliate program by detecting and managing suspicious activities, such as self-referrals, unusual referring sites, and abnormal conversion rates. It provides you with tools to monitor and flag potential fraud, ensuring the integrity of your affiliate program.

### What happens if I have the Allow Own Referrals addon active?

If the Allow Own Referrals addon is active, the Self-Referrals setting in the Fraud Prevention addon will automatically be set to “Allow.” This disables the options to flag or reject self-referrals. If you want to use these options, you’ll need to deactivate the Allow Own Referrals addon.

### How does the Referring Sites feature work?

The Referring Sites feature checks whether the URL that referred the visit matches the affiliate’s registered website URL. You can choose to allow all referrals, flag referrals from non-matching URLs as potentially fraudulent, or reject referrals from non-matching URLs entirely.

### What does the Conversion Rate feature do?

The Conversion Rate feature monitors the ratio of referrals to visits for each affiliate, ensuring it falls within a defined range. If an affiliate’s conversion rate is outside the acceptable limits, the visits and referrals can be flagged for further review.

### What does it mean when a referral is flagged?

When a referral is flagged, it’s marked as potentially fraudulent based on the settings you’ve configured. Flagged referrals are still eligible for payout but are highlighted in your dashboard for you to review and investigate if needed.

### How can I review which setting triggered a flagged referral?

In **AffiliateWP » Referrals**, flagged referrals are marked with a red flag icon. Hover over this icon to see a message explaining which fraud prevention setting triggered the flag. This helps you quickly understand why the referral was flagged and take appropriate action.

### Can I completely prevent affiliates from earning commissions on their own purchases?

Yes, by setting the Self-Referrals option to “Reject,” you can block affiliates from earning commissions on their own purchases. This ensures that self-referrals do not generate any commissions.

---

That’s it! The Fraud Prevention addon provides essential tools to help you monitor and prevent affiliate fraud. By carefully configuring the settings for self-referrals, referring sites, and conversion rates, you can ensure that your affiliate program operates smoothly and securely. These features allow you to detect and manage suspicious activities, helping to maintain the integrity and profitability of your affiliate program.

pages.title: LearnDash
pages.content:
AffiliateWP’s integration with LearnDash allows you to easily set up and manage an affiliate program for your online courses. By connecting AffiliateWP with LearnDash, you can track referrals, set customizable commission structures, and provide affiliates with detailed analytics to help drive course sales. This seamless integration simplifies the process, enabling you to pay affiliates efficiently and grow your course offerings with the power of affiliate marketing.

**In This Article**

- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [LearnDash Referrals](#learndash-referrals)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)

## Configuration

To enable support for [LearnDash](https://www.learndash.com/), navigate to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Integrations***,*and check the box next to **LearnDash**:

![LearnDash Integration](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/learndash.png)

Once enabled, all courses purchased through LearnDash via **Stripe Connect**payments****(PayPal and other payment gateways are not supported at this time), and tracking an affiliate will automatically generate referrals.

## LearnDash Referrals

In **AffiliateWP » Referrals***,*the **Reference****column displays the transaction number in link form:

![LearnDash referral example in the Referrals list](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/reference-column-2-767x95.png)

Clicking on the link in the ****Reference****column of the referral will take you directly to the transaction entry in LearnDash:

![LearnDash transaction displayed after clicking the number in the referral's Reference column](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Python-course-767x214.png)

If you are using LearnDash with Easy Digital Downloads or WooCommerce and their LearnDash addons, you do not need to enable the LearnDash integration for AffiliateWP, you would need to enable the Easy Digital Download or WooCommerce integrations.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which payment gateways are supported for tracking referrals in LearnDash?

Currently, AffiliateWP’s LearnDash integration supports tracking referrals for courses purchased via Stripe Connect payments. Other payment gateways, such as PayPal, are not supported at this time.

### Can I set up an affiliate program for LearnDash without using an e-commerce plugin?

Yes, AffiliateWP integrates directly with LearnDash, allowing you to set up an affiliate program without the need for additional e-commerce plugins like WooCommerce or Easy Digital Downloads. This direct integration simplifies the process of managing affiliate referrals for your courses

### How can affiliates promote my LearnDash courses?

Affiliates can promote your LearnDash courses by sharing their unique referral URLs. When someone purchases a course through these links, the affiliate earns a commission based on the structure you’ve set up in AffiliateWP.

### Are there additional tools to enhance my LearnDash affiliate program?

Yes, AffiliateWP provides various addons to enhance your affiliate program, such as the [Affiliate Portal](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/affiliate-portal-installation-and-usage/)for a custom dashboard experience and [Custom Affiliate Slugs](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/custom-affiliate-slugs-installation-and-usage/) for personalized link structures. These tools can help attract, manage, and incentivize affiliates more effectively.

---

Integrating LearnDash with AffiliateWP enables you to effectively manage affiliate commissions for course purchases made through LearnDash. By activating the LearnDash integration within AffiliateWP’s settings, referrals are automatically generated for courses bought via Stripe Connect payments. This seamless integration simplifies the tracking and management of affiliate referrals, enhancing your ability to monitor and reward affiliates for their contributions to your course sales.

pages.title: Affiliate Email Summaries
pages.content:
Affiliate Email Summaries is a feature that will send emails direct to affiliates that show how they’ve performed for the past 30 days, starting on the day the feature is fully activated (including installing and configuring [WP Mail SMTP](https://wpmailsmtp.com)). To be eligible, the affiliate must have an **Active** status and registered for a minimum of 30 days.  After the initial email, they will receive a new email summary every 30 days.

Once the setting is enabled, they will begin sending within approximately 15 minutes.

**Note**: We schedule individual affiliate summary emails to begin sending once per minute after the activation. For example, if you have 10 affiliates, it will take about 10 minutes for all emails to be sent — if you have 500 affiliates, it might take up to 8 hours for emails to reach all 500 affiliates.

---

### How To Enable This Feature

To enable this feature, navigate to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Emails**, check the box next to **Affiliate Email Summaries**, and save your changes at the bottom of the screen.

![AffiliateWP - Settings - Emails screen showing the Affiliate Email Summaries setting](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/affiliate-email-summaries-setting-1024x340.png)

#### Affiliate Email Summary Examples

To see a preview of how the emails will appear, you can click the **View Example**link as shown in the noted image area above.  The emails will include the following information:

- Total Earnings
- Total Referrals
- Total Visits
- Conversion Rate
- Top 10 Highest Converting URLs

**Note:** At this time, this feature is not supported in WordPress Multisite so this setting will not be available.

#### Requires WP Mail SMTP

Once enabled, if you do not already have [WP Mail SMTP](https://wpmailsmtp.com/) enabled and configured, you will receive a notice at the top of the **Email** settings screen to do so:

![](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/email-summaries-1024x262.png)

Once [WP Mail SMTP](https://wpmailsmtp.com/) is installed, activated [with any mailer](https://wpmailsmtp.com/docs/a-complete-guide-to-wp-mail-smtp-mailers/) (other than the default), and configured, you will be good to go to start sending affiliate email summaries.

**Note:** If the **Default** mailer is selected, or WP Mail SMTP is not active, emails will not be sent. This is required since many web servers have limits to the number of emails that can be sent within a specific time period. WP Mail SMTP Pro helps ensure reliable email delivery, including the tools to troubleshoot should any emails not get delivered as expected.

pages.title: Troubleshooting Issues With AffiliateWP
pages.content:
Are you experiencing issues with AffiliateWP? Our support team is here to help you troubleshoot any questions, errors, or unexpected behavior you might encounter while using AffiliateWP or its addons. However, to provide you with the most efficient solution, we need your assistance in diagnosing the problem.

In this guide, we’ll discuss a few key questions to consider before reaching out to our support team. Addressing these questions might help you identify and resolve the issue on your own, saving time and effort.

In This Article

- [Is AffiliateWP Fully Updated?](#aioseo-is-affiliatewp-fully-updated)
- [Does Your Site Use Optimization or Caching?](#aioseo-does-your-site-use-optimization-or-caching)
- [Could Another Plugin Be Causing a Conflict?](#aioseo-could-another-plugin-be-causing-a-conflict)
- [Do You Still Need Support?](#aioseo-do-you-still-need-support-after-steps-1-3)

## Is AffiliateWP Fully Updated?

One of the first steps in troubleshooting any issue is ensuring that your AffiliateWP plugin is up-to-date. Our team regularly releases updates that improve functionality and address potential issues. To check if AffiliateWP is updated:

- Verify that your AffiliateWP [license key](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/how-to-verify-your-affiliatewp-license/) is active on your site.
- Go to the **Plugins** section in your WordPress dashboard. If an update is available for AffiliateWP, click **Update** to install it.

You can view the changes included in each update by checking the [AffiliateWP changelog](https://affiliatewp.com/changelog/).

## Does Your Site Use Optimization or Caching?

Sometimes, optimization or caching plugins can interfere with AffiliateWP’s tracking functionality, leading to issues such as visits or referrals not being tracked correctly. If you suspect this might be the case:

- Review your caching plugin’s settings to see if it’s excluding AffiliateWP’s tracking cookies and affiliate-area pages.
- We maintain a [documentation](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/does-affiliatewp-work-with-caching/) that lists known caching plugins and services, along with instructions on how to configure them to work smoothly with AffiliateWP.

## Could Another Plugin Be Causing a Conflict?

Plugin conflicts are another common source of issues. If AffiliateWP isn’t functioning as expected, another plugin might be interfering. To check for conflicts:

- Disable all other plugins and see if the problem persists. If AffiliateWP starts working correctly, re-enable your plugins one by one to identify the conflicting plugin.
- WPBeginner offers a guide to [troubleshooting WordPress errors](http://www.wpbeginner.com/beginners-guide/beginners-guide-to-troubleshooting-wordpress-errors-step-by-step/) that can walk you through this process.

If you identify a conflicting plugin, contacting its support team or author is usually the next best step.

For advice on choosing high-quality WordPress plugins that are less likely to cause conflicts, refer to [WPBeginner’s guide on this topic](http://www.wpbeginner.com/beginners-guide/how-to-choose-the-best-wordpress-plugin/).

> 

## Do You Still Need Support?

If you’ve gone through the first three steps and still haven’t resolved the issue, it’s time to reach out to AffiliateWP Support. To help us assist you as quickly and effectively as possible:

- Be specific about the problem and what you’re trying to achieve with AffiliateWP. Include any relevant URLs.
- Enable debug mode in **AffiliateWP » Settings » Advanced » Privacy & Logging**. This will collect details like error messages that can give us a clearer picture of what’s happening on your site.

![Debug mode](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/debug-mode-1024x285.png)

---

That’s it! By following these troubleshooting steps, you may be able to resolve the issue on your own. If not, the information you gather will be invaluable in helping our support team provide the best possible assistance.

We’re here to ensure that your experience with AffiliateWP is smooth and successful. Don’t hesitate to [reach out](https://affiliatewp.com/contact/) if you need further help.
headings: Does Your Site Use Optimization or Caching?
Could Another Plugin Be Causing a Conflict?

pages.title: Creating Affiliate Terms of Use Page
pages.content:
Need to create a Terms of Use page for your affiliate program? The AffiliateWP Terms of Use Generator simplifies this process by providing a customizable template.

In this guide, we’ll show you how to access the generator, customize the template, and publish your Terms of Use page.

In This Article

- [How to Use the Terms of Use Generator](#how-to-use-the-terms-of-use-generator)
- [Customizing and Publishing Your Terms of Use](#customizing-and-publishing-your-terms-of-use)
- [Editing the Terms of Use Page Later](#editing-the-terms-of-use-page-later)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)

## How to Use the Terms of Use Generator

To get started, go to **AffiliateWP » Settings » Affiliates** in your WordPress dashboard. In the **Terms of Use** section, you’ll see a link labeled **“Create one using a template”**. Click this link to open the Terms of Use Generator.

![Terms of use link location in Affiliates settings page](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/terms-of-use-link-1024x351.png)

Alternatively, you can access the generator directly by navigating to **AffiliateWP » Tools » Terms of Use Generator**.

![](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/create-terms-of-use-page-767x563.png)

Once the generator opens, you’ll notice that the **Company Name** field is automatically populated with your site name. This name will be used throughout the template to reference your business. If necessary, you can adjust the name to better reflect your program or branding. A preview of the Terms of Use will be displayed, giving you a chance to review the text before proceeding.

## Customizing and Publishing Your Terms of Use

After generating the Terms of Use page, you’ll be redirected to the WordPress page editor. Here, you can make additional edits to tailor the content to your specific requirements. Feel free to adjust the language, add program-specific details, or include any legal disclaimers required for your jurisdiction.

![Publish terms of use page](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/publish-terms-767x305.png)

Once you’ve reviewed and made all necessary changes, click **Publish** to make the page live on your site. This will provide affiliates with a clear understanding of the terms and conditions of your program.

## Editing the Terms of Use Page Later

If you need to edit your Terms of Use page in the future, you can find it in the **Pages** section of your WordPress dashboard. Simply locate the page titled **Affiliate Terms of Use** and open it for editing. This allows you to keep the content up-to-date as your program evolves.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I customize the Terms of Use template?

Yes, after generating the page, you’ll be redirected to the WordPress editor. From there, you can modify the content as needed to match your program’s specific requirements or legal needs.

### Where can I find the Terms of Use page after publishing?

Once published, the Terms of Use page is stored in the **Pages** section of your WordPress dashboard. Look for the page titled **Affiliate Terms of Use** to edit or update it later.

### What if I want to use a different name instead of the default site name?

The generator automatically uses your site name for the **Company Name** field. However, you can adjust this field while using the generator to reflect your preferred name before creating the page.

### Is the Terms of Use Generator mandatory for AffiliateWP?

No, the generator is optional. If you prefer, you can create your own Terms of Use page manually without using the generator.

### What happens if I delete the Terms of Use page?

If you delete the page, you’ll need to regenerate it using the Terms of Use Generator or create a new page manually. Deleted pages cannot be recovered unless you restore them from the WordPress trash.

---

That’s it! The AffiliateWP Terms of Use Generator makes it easy to create a professional and customizable Terms of Use page for your affiliate program. By following the steps outlined above, you can ensure your affiliates understand their responsibilities while protecting your program with clear terms and conditions. If updates are needed, you can easily edit the page through the WordPress Pages section at any time.

pages.title: [affiliate_conversion_script] shortcode
pages.content:
Do you need to track referrals on custom success pages where purchases, signups, or other conversions occur? The **[affiliate_conversion_script]** shortcode allows you to generate referral records when visitors complete an action on your site after arriving via an affiliate referral link. This is useful for tracking successful transactions outside of AffiliateWP’s standard integrations, ensuring that affiliates are properly credited for referred conversions.

This guide explains how to use the 
```
[affiliate_conversion_script]
```

shortcode, its parameters, and how to dynamically pass values through query strings.

In This Article

- [How the [affiliate_conversion_script] Shortcode Works](#how-the-affiliate_conversion_script-shortcode-works)
- [Configuring the Shortcode Parameters](#configuring-the-shortcode-parameters)- [Example Shortcode Usage](#example-shortcode-usage)
- [Key Considerations When Using This Shortcode](#important-considerations)
- [Passing Dynamic Values Through URLs](#passing-dynamic-values-through-urls)- [Example: Passing a Purchase Amount in the URL](#example-passing-a-purchase-amount-in-the-url)
- [Example: Passing Multiple Parameters in the URL](#example-passing-multiple-parameters-in-the-url)

## How the [affiliate_conversion_script] Shortcode Works

When a visitor clicks an affiliate referral link and successfully completes a purchase, signup, or another defined conversion action, you can place the 
```
[affiliate_conversion_script]
```

shortcode on your **“success” page** to generate a referral for the affiliate. This ensures that even custom checkout or signup flows outside of traditional eCommerce integrations can still track referrals properly.

To use the shortcode effectively, add it to the **thank you** or **confirmation** page where visitors land after completing a transaction.

## Configuring the Shortcode Parameters

The **[affiliate_conversion_script]** shortcode supports multiple parameters to define referral details:

- **Amount** – Defines the total purchase amount the referral is based on. The affiliate’s referral rate will determine the commission from this amount.
- **Description** – Adds a custom description to the referral record for tracking purposes.
- **Context** – Identifies the context of the referral (useful for tracking multiple forms or purchase types).
- **Reference** – A unique reference ID for the transaction, such as a user ID or order number.
- **Status** – Sets the referral status. Options include **pending, unpaid, paid,** or **rejected**. By default, it is set to **pending**.
- **Type** – Defines the referral type. Options include **sale, lead,** or **opt-in**. By default, it is set to **sale**.

### Example Shortcode Usage

```
[affiliate_conversion_script amount="10" description="My Description" context="Contact Form" reference="1234" status="pending" type="lead"]
```

This example creates a referral with:

- A $10 purchase amount
- The description “My Description”
- The context “Contact Form”
- The reference ID 1234
- A status of pending
- A referral type of lead

## Key Considerations When Using This Shortcode

To ensure proper functionality, keep these key points in mind:

- **The shortcode should only be placed on success pages** – It should be added to the confirmation page customers land on after completing a purchase, signup, or another conversion event.
- **A referral can only be created once per visitor while the tracking cookie is active** – If a visitor returns while their affiliate tracking cookie is still valid, no new referral will be generated.
- **Shortcode formatting is critical** – Ensure spaces are correctly placed between parameters. Improper formatting may cause blank values or a zero referral amount.
- **Coupons are not supported** – Discount codes or coupons do not affect referral amounts when using this shortcode. If you need coupon-based tracking, consider using one of AffiliateWP’s supported integrations.

## Passing Dynamic Values Through URLs

You can dynamically pass values to the **** shortcode using query strings in the URL. This is useful for automatically setting the referral amount and other parameters based on purchase details.

### Example: Passing a Purchase Amount in the URL

```
https://yoursite.com/thanks/?amount=100
```

- Here, yoursite.com/thanks/ is the purchase confirmation page where the shortcode is placed.
- amount=100 dynamically sets the referral amount to $100.

### Example: Passing Multiple Parameters in the URL

```
https://yoursite.com/thanks/?amount=100&description=My%20Description&context=Contact%20Form&reference=1234&status=pending&type=lead
```

This URL dynamically assigns values to amount, description, context, reference, status, and type based on the parameters passed in the query string.

- Dynamic values **cannot overwrite** parameters already set inside the shortcode. If you define an **amount** in the shortcode, the value passed in the URL will not replace it.
- Use **URL encoding** (e.g., replace spaces with **%20**) to ensure proper formatting in query strings.

---

That’s it! The **[affiliate_conversion_script]** shortcode is a powerful tool for tracking custom conversions on success pages. By placing it on your checkout or signup confirmation pages, you can ensure that affiliates are credited for referrals even when using custom transaction processes.
headings: Key Considerations When Using This Shortcode
Example: Passing a Purchase Amount in the URL
Example: Passing Multiple Parameters in the URL

pages.title: [affiliate_coupons] shortcode
pages.content:
Want to display an [affiliate’s assigned coupons](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/affiliate-coupon-tracking/) on a WordPress page? The **[affiliate_coupons]** shortcode allows you to showcase affiliate-specific discount codes along with their values. If an affiliate has coupons assigned to them, this shortcode will generate an HTML table listing all available coupons.

While AffiliateWP automatically displays an affiliate’s assigned coupons in the Affiliate Area, you may want to use this shortcode to show coupons elsewhere on your site.

In This Article

- [How the [affiliate_coupons] Shortcode Works](#how-the-affiliate_coupons-shortcode-works)
- [Using the [affiliate_coupons] Shortcode](#using-the-affiliate_coupons-shortcode)

## How the [affiliate_coupons] Shortcode Works

The 
```
[affiliate_coupons]
```

 shortcode pulls an affiliate’s assigned coupons from supported integrations and displays them in an HTML table. This makes it easy for affiliates to view and share their available discount codes with potential customers.

Currently, the shortcode works with the following integrations:

- [WooCommerce](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/woocommerce/)
- [Easy Digital Downloads](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/easy-digital-downloads/)
- [MemberPress](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/memberpress/)

If no coupons are assigned to the affiliate, the shortcode won’t output anything.

## Using the [affiliate_coupons] Shortcode

To display an affiliate’s coupons, simply place the following shortcode on any WordPress page or post:

```
[affiliate_coupons]
```

This will generate an HTML table listing all assigned coupons along with their discount amounts. The shortcode can be used within:

- The Affiliate Area (though AffiliateWP already displays coupons there by default)
- A custom dashboard page for affiliates
- A dedicated coupon page for easy reference

---

That’s it! The 
```
[affiliate_coupons]
```

 shortcode is a simple yet effective way to display affiliate-specific discount codes on any WordPress page. While the [Affiliate Area](https://affiliatewp.com/docs/creating-the-affiliate-area/) already includes coupon details, this shortcode offers flexibility in where and how you present this information to your affiliates.

pages.title: [affiliate_creatives] shortcode
pages.content:
Want to display your affiliate creatives on any page of your WordPress site? The **[affiliate_creatives]** shortcode makes it easy to showcase all available creatives from **AffiliateWP » Creatives**.

Creatives are promotional materials, such as banners and text links, that affiliates can use to promote your products or services. By using this shortcode, you can provide affiliates with an easy way to access and use these marketing assets.

In This Article

- [How the [affiliate_creatives] Shortcode Works](#how-the-affiliate_creatives-shortcode-works)
- [Using the [affiliate_creatives] Shortcode](#using-the-affiliate_creatives-shortcode)

## How the [affiliate_creatives] Shortcode Works

When placed on a WordPress page or post, the **[affiliate_creatives]** shortcode will automatically display all approved creatives from **AffiliateWP » Creatives**. Affiliates can then copy the links or download the banners for their promotional efforts.

Only logged-in affiliates can see the creatives. If a visitor or a non-affiliate user views the page, they won’t see any content.

## Using the [affiliate_creatives] Shortcode

To display all creatives, simply add the following shortcode to any page or post:

```
[affiliate_creatives]
```

This will generate a list of creatives that affiliates can use to promote your brand.

---

That’s it! The **[affiliate_creatives]** shortcode is a powerful tool for making your marketing assets more accessible to affiliates. Whether you want to create a dedicated creatives page or enhance the Affiliate Area, this shortcode allows you to display promotional materials in a structured and convenient way.

This shortcode is particularly useful for encouraging users to **sign up for your affiliate program**, displaying promotional messages, or providing information only relevant to non-affiliates. pages.title: [affiliate_creative] shortcode
pages.content:
The 
```
[affiliate_creative]
```

 shortcode allows you to display a **specific creative** from **AffiliateWP » Creatives** on any page of your website. This is useful when you want to showcase a particular banner, text link, or marketing material for affiliates in a specific section of your website instead of displaying all creatives at once.

In This Article

- [Using [affiliate_creative] Shortcode](#affiliate_creative-shortcode)
- [Finding the Creative ID](#finding-the-creative-id)
- [Example Use Cases](#example-use-cases)- [Displaying a Specific Banner Ad on a Custom Page](#displaying-a-specific-banner-ad-on-a-custom-page)
- [Embedding a Custom Text Link in a Blog Post](#embedding-a-custom-text-link-in-a-blog-post)

## Using [affiliate_creative] Shortcode

To use this shortcode, simply specify the **creative ID** within the shortcode as shown below:

```
[affiliate_creative id="123"]
```

In this example, **123** represents the **ID of the creative** you want to display.

## Finding the Creative ID

To locate the creative ID:

1. Navigate to **AffiliateWP » Creatives** in your WordPress admin dashboard.
2. Find the creative you want to display.
3. Copy the **ID number** associated with that creative from the URL bar.
4. Use this ID in the shortcode to display the specific creative.

## Example Use Cases

### Displaying a Specific Banner Ad on a Custom Page

If you want to display a **single banner creative** on a landing page, you can use:

```
[affiliate_creative id="45"]
```

This will embed the **creative with ID 45**, ensuring that only that specific banner is shown.

### Embedding a Custom Text Link in a Blog Post

If you want to display a **text-based creative** in a blog post promoting your affiliate program, use:

```
[affiliate_creative id="78"]
```

This will output the **text link creative with ID 78**, making it easy for affiliates to copy and share.

- **Affiliates must be logged in** to view the creative. If they are not logged in, they will not see anything.
- This shortcode is different from 
```
[affiliate_creatives]
```

, which displays **all available creatives**.

---

The 
```
[affiliate_creative]
```

 shortcode is an excellent tool for displaying **a single creative** instead of all available creatives. Whether you want to embed a **specific banner ad, text link, or other promotional material**, this shortcode makes it easy to place creatives **exactly where you need them** for affiliates.

AffiliateWP has a simple opt-in form to allow affiliates to promote email signups for a site owner wishing to grow their email marketing lists. The form is displayed with the  **[opt_in]**shortcode. In addition, this introduces a new [referral type](/docs/referral-types/) with the value **Opt-in**.

**Usage:**

```
[opt_in]
```

**Display:**

![Opt-In Form example](https://affiliatewp.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/file-qmZRL8GICp.png)

If you’d like to redirect users after they submit an opt-in form to a specific page, use the redirect parameter of the shortcode:

```
[opt_in redirect="http://yoursite.com/new-page"]
```

If a **non-affiliate or a logged-out user** views the page, the content inside the shortcode will not be visible. ## Example Use Case ### Providing Exclusive Affiliate Banners and Links If you want to display marketing materials only to logged-in affiliates, use: ``` [affiliate_content] Here are your exclusive banners and referral links! The ``` [affiliate_content] ``` shortcode is a simple yet powerful way to **control access** to affiliate-exclusive content.
